description: A coordinated disinformation campaign using highly personalized synthetic media targets multiple EU member states’ local elections, exploiting open-weight models to generate region-specific narratives. The campaign is traced to a non-state actor using anonymized cloud infrastructure, and while no election is annulled, several are delayed due to legal challenges over vote integrity. Public trust in digital civic space erodes further.

An international consortium of academic labs and independent AI safety researchers announces the formation of the Open Assurance Network, a decentralized framework for auditing and monitoring open-weight models using adversarial testing and red-teaming pools. The network begins publishing risk scores for prominent open models, gaining traction among developers and regulators. While not binding, it becomes a de facto standard for open model trustworthiness in the absence of official oversight.
